subject: Phoebe-70B onboarding + safe-pin exception request
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@openbench.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Phoebe-70B release & onboarding materials

Hi Markus / Laura,

Quick intro — OpenBench is publishing the Phoebe family (70B) today. We have three primary runtime artifacts: phoebe-70b-fp16 (baseline fp16 weights), phoebe-70b-q8 (8-bit quantized), and phoebe-70b-slim (parameter-reduced 36B variant). Attached are the perf matrix and a short model card.

We'd like Redwood to onboard phoebe-70b-fp16 into the hosted catalog and make the fp16 variant available in Dedicated by next week. A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you run your standard compat checks (tokenizer parity, kv-cache correctness, logits-stability) and share an expected perf profile?
- If your regression tests flag small diffs (e.g., tokenization offsets or mild score shifts), would Redwood consider a temporary pin to the fp16 variant in prod for 14 days while we iterate? We plan to ship a small patch to the tokenizer within 72 hours if issues surface.

I attached: phoebe70b-perf-matrix.csv, phoebe70b-model-card.pdf.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Model Partnerships, OpenBench
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@openbench.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phoebe-70B release & onboarding materials

Thanks Samira — and congrats on the release. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Hannah (reliability) so we can triage. A few immediate asks from our side:

1) Compatibility checklist: can you confirm tokenizer repo and SHA, and whether you have a migration path if special tokens change?
2) Variant pin: we need a formal pin-exception request to keep the fp16 variant pinned for 14 days in hosted while we run regressions. Please attach a short statement of risk and rollback plan (for legal and compliance).
3) Performance expectations: rough RPS and p99 latency at 1 and 4 token batch sizes — we use that for capacity planning.

If Dev's initial checks look okay we'll open INF-4721 and propose a controlled canary (10% traffic for 24h) with automatic rollback on defined regression signals. Hannah — can you confirm the SLO window we should use for the canary?

Markus
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Morning — did a quick skim of the perf CSV and ran a tiny tokenization parity check against our harness. Notes: 

- Tokenizer: repo/sha not included in CSV — Samira, can you share? We saw one edge case where the new tokenizer emits an extra BOS token for prompt variations with leading whitespace; that causes off-by-one in a small set of prompts (will surface as misaligned completions).
- KV cache: fp16 path looks compatible with our KV layout; q8 variant requires the new quant-dequant shim (we can add that but it changes fill/evict behavior).
- Throughput: fp16 baseline looks comparable to similar fp16 70B models — roughly 6–8 tok/ms on an A100-like profile in our local run (12B context, ephemeral batch sizes). Expect ~12–18% higher memory compared to a heavily-quantized path.

Proposal for safe onboarding:
1) Create a pin exception (pin-phoebe70b-20260220-v1) that pins hosted production routes to phoebe-70b-fp16 for 14 days. This is a soft pin: our routing will honor it and skip automatic fallback to q8 during that window.
2) Run the regression suite (deterministic evals + 30 curated prompts for safety/behavioral checks) in a canary: 10% traffic, 24h. Failure criteria: increase in hallucination metric >2% or >3% degraded ROUGE on the core eval set.
3) If minor tokenizer offset found, OpenBench provides a tokenizer patch (expected <72h) and we re-run the evals; full rollback if degradation persists after patch.

I've attached a filled pin-exception-form.pdf and opened INF-4721 with the checklist. I'll also add a short script to run the small parity harness we used.

- Dev

Thanks Dev — good summary. From a product POV we need:

- Canary metrics template filled (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost per 1M tokens, user quality sample pass rate). I attached canary-metrics-template.xlsx.
- Explicit rollback criteria (Dev suggested hallucination + rouge thresholds; add latency spike >25% and error-rate >1%).
- Cost delta estimate for both Hosted (per token charge) and Dedicated (reserved capacity impact). Even a back-of-envelope delta is fine.

Operational timeline: if we get the tokenizer SHA and the filled canary template today, we can schedule canary for Mon 02/23 and decide go/no-go by end of day Tue 02/24. Legal side — we might need a short addendum if OpenBench wants to block fallback to quantized variants; Samira, can you confirm that request in writing so our compliance team can review?

Laura
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few quick replies:

- Tokenizer: repo is https://github.com/openbench/phoebe-tokenizer, SHA: a1b2c3d4e5. The extra BOS behavior is an intentional early change; we can branch a compatibility shim and push a patch within 48–72h.
- Pin request: we confirm we request a temporary pin of phoebe-70b-fp16 for 14 days to avoid automatic fallback to q8 while the shim lands. We will provide a written addendum for compliance.
- Registry: weights are available at model-registry://phoebe/70b/fp16/v1 and we will upload an FP16+Q8 bundle to the registry by EOD.

I'll attach the addendum and the updated model bundle once available. Happy to join the canary kickoff on Monday.

Best,
Samira
